label: copy phase, 3rd+ output, mid/late absolute step, copied input in {z,n,g,e,3,o,j,x}
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), and essentially only from the 3rd output on (recall_idx >= 2). It is concentrated at absolute steps t=11-13 and in long sequences (L=8-9 carry about 73% of the mass). Within that window the input token matters a lot: fed-back z (4.5x lift, the strongest examples are z at about 0.9-1.0 of max), then n, g, e, 3, and less so o, j, x. Output token also shifts the rate (3, l, b, h are the highest). Activations often come in runs over several consecutive copy steps. The copy-phase position gate alone has about 100% recall but 14% precision. Adding the token set gives dev F1 of about 0.50 (precision 0.44, recall 0.58, mass recall 0.69). Requiring both input and output token sets raises precision to 0.70 but cuts recall to 0.21. The token weighting looks graded rather than a clean set, so this is incomplete.
